label: Accidental
title: Accidental/spontaneous integration events.

label: Normally_Non-integrating_Virus
title: Virus families that are more likely the result of spontaneous integration rather than Retrotranposition.

label: Artifact
title: Elements often found in cloning vectors that may contaminate sequencing projects.

label: Interspersed_Repeat
title: A repetitive sequence with copies interspersed throughout an organisms genome.

label: Pseudogene
title: Duplications of existing genes in an organism.

label: RNA
title: Non-translated, small RNA genes often found in high copy number.

label: rRNA
title: Copies of a ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene or pseudogene.

label: snRNA
title: Copies of a small nuclear RNA (snRNA) gene or pseudogene.
definition: Small nuclear RNAs include 7SK RNA and the U1 to U13. They are dependent on external promoters and are theferore much less frequently involved in the creation of a SINE

label: tRNA
title: Copies of a transfer RNA (tRNA) gene or pseudogene.
definition: In mammals,  tRNAs copies can occur in relatively large numbers (up to a thousand copies) The boundary between a large number of accidentally retroposed or otherwise duplicated (pseudo)genes and a low copy number SINE (selected on its ability to propagate) is nebulous

label: Transposable_Element
title: Families that are the direct result of transposition events.

label: Class_II_DNA_Transposition
title: Elements that do not require an RNA intermediate in their transposition lifecycle.

label: Casposon
title: Archaeal and bacterial mobile elements at the origin of CRISPR-Cas immunity.

label: Helicase
title: Circular ssDNA Intermediate.

label: Transposase
title: DNA transposons with terminal inverted repeats ranging from 6 bp to many kb.

label: Academ
title: Academ superfamily of  DNA transposons.
definition: Found in metazoans and fungi, autonomous Academ elements encode a ca 1.5 kb protein containing an XPG exonuclease domain, a Cys8 zinc finger, and a DDE transposase domain unlike those of others. Termini tend to be TAG…CTA and a 3 bp target site is duplicated.

label: Academ-1
title: First described family of Academ DNA transposon.

label: Academ-2

label: Academ-H
title: Family of Academ transposons described in rust fungi.

label: SINE
title: Short LINE-dependent retroposons with an internal (usually pol III) promoter.
definition: The median length of described SINEs is ca. 250 bp ±130 bp SD. The canonical SINE has a tRNA 5' end with the internal promoter, a core of unknown function shared with multiple other SINE families, a 3' end identical to that of the LINE responsible for its mobility, and a simple repeat tail. A few SINEs have a LINE-derived internal pol II promoter, and many lack either or both the core and LINE-derived regions.
